title: Point realization of coefficient-compatible dual exchange squares
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Use the point categories and fibre functors $F_\Lambda=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and constructibility and finite Tor amplitude of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Put $D_\Lambda C=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_{s,\Lambda})$, with $\omega_{s,\Lambda}=R\operatorname{id}_s^!\Lambda_s$, using [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Write $j_{\Lambda,C}:F_\Lambda D_\Lambda C\xrightarrow{\sim}(F_\Lambda C)^\vee$ for the specified point identification of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex], where $c^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(c,\Lambda)$.

Let $C,T\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$ and $e:D_\Lambda C\xrightarrow{\sim}T$. Then
$$g=F_\Lambda(e)\circ j_{\Lambda,C}^{-1}:(F_\Lambda C)^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}F_\Lambda T$$
is an isomorphism, natural and compatible with shifts whenever the family $e$ has those properties.

Let $Q_s$ be one of the stipulated point coefficient changes: finite reduction $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ with $1\leq m\leq n$, integral reduction $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$, integral scalar extension for a finite coefficient-field extension, rationalization, or scalar extension at a common finite field stage. Let $q$ denote its module-complex counterpart. Let $C',T'\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda')$, $u:Q_sC\xrightarrow{\sim}C'$, $v:Q_sT\to T'$, and $e':D_{\Lambda'}C'\xrightarrow{\sim}T'$. Use the canonical dual comparison $\delta_{Q,C}:Q_sD_\Lambda C\to D_{\Lambda'}Q_sC$ and module-dual comparison $b_{Q,c}:q(c^\vee)\to(qc)^\vee$ of [lem-pod-point-duality-coefficient-compatibility]. Assume the site square
$$v\circ Q_s(e)=e'\circ D_{\Lambda'}(u^{-1})\circ\delta_{Q,C}.$$
For $B\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$ let $t_{Q,B}:q(F_\Lambda B)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\Lambda'}Q_sB$ be the canonical natural sections/coefficient map specified in [lem-pod-point-duality-coefficient-compatibility]: the derived-reduction sections comparison for integral reduction; the inverse of the sections scalar comparison $\varphi$ for integral or common-stage extension; the defining rationalization comparison; and the tensoring-sections map for finite quotients. These use the tensor and unit constraints of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. Put $c=F_\Lambda C$, $c'=F_{\Lambda'}C'$, $w=F_{\Lambda'}(u)\circ t_{Q,C}$ and $V=F_{\Lambda'}(v)\circ t_{Q,T}$. For $g'=F_{\Lambda'}(e')\circ j_{\Lambda',C'}^{-1}$ the coefficient-complex square is exactly
$$V\circ q(g)=g'\circ(w^{-1})^\vee\circ b_{Q,c}.$$
Here $(w^{-1})^\vee:(qc)^\vee\to(c')^\vee$ is precomposition by $w^{-1}$. The assertion applies in particular when $u$ is a compact-support coefficient comparison; it uses its actual map, rather than replacing $Q_sC$ by $C'$ as an equality.

proof.text: The point lemmas cited here are stated in the conventions of [def-pod-conventions]; apply them with $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, which is smooth, separated of finite type and geometrically connected of pure dimension $0$, so that $X=s$ and $a_X=\operatorname{id}_s$, exceptional-adjoint admissible at every finite coefficient stage by [lem-sf-point-identity-admissibility]. Use the specified point-dualizing identification $j$. Its naturality is the natural Hom-complex isomorphism $h\mapsto(x\mapsto h(1\otimes x))$ of [lem-pod-point-derived-hom-evaluation] at finite and integral coefficients, followed by the fixed identification $\omega_s\cong\Lambda_s$. For a map $f:B\to C$, precomposition gives $j_B F(Df)=(Ff)^\vee j_C$. The same formula is natural for localized and common-stage morphisms by [lem-pod-point-hom-rational-descent]; its hypothesis that $R\mathcal Hom(C,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})$ is the constructible finite-projective Hom model is [lem-pod-point-completed-evaluation]. These comparisons respect shifts: on Hom complexes the formula evaluates the same homogeneous component before or after reindexing, and sections, being degreewise, preserve the signed shift differential. Rationalization and common-stage extension preserve that equality. The fibre functors commute with shifts by [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence].

proof.text: Functoriality sends $e^{-1}$ to an inverse of $F(e)$. Thus $g=F(e)j_C^{-1}$ is invertible, with inverse $j_C F(e^{-1})$. For any naturality square of the family $e$, apply $F$ and conjugate its dual-source side by the natural $j$ of step 1; cancellation gives precisely the naturality square for $g$. Apply the same cancellation to its shift square, using step 1, to obtain shift compatibility whenever $e$ has it.

proof.text:
Abbreviate $F=F_\Lambda$, $F'=F_{\Lambda'}$, $t_B=t_{Q,B}$, $j=j_{\Lambda,C}$, and $j_{QC}=j_{\Lambda',Q_sC}$. Naturality of the specified $t$ gives $t_T q(F(e))=F'(Q_s(e))t_{D C}$. Apply $F'$ to the assumed site square and substitute this identity to obtain
$$Vq(g)=F'(e')F'(D(u^{-1}))F'(\delta_{Q,C})t_{D C}q(j^{-1}).$$
All $t$ here are the actual comparisons of [lem-pod-point-duality-coefficient-compatibility], including its finite-quotient map; no independent choice of an isomorphism is made.

source.place: Second paragraph: applying the point fibre and identifying the coefficient-change square through the point-dualizing identification.

proof.text:
By step 1, $j_{C'}F'(D(u^{-1}))=(F'(u^{-1}))^\vee j_{QC}$. The coefficient-duality identity of [lem-pod-point-duality-coefficient-compatibility], composed on its source with $q(j^{-1})$, gives
$$t_C^\vee j_{QC}F'(\delta_{Q,C})t_{D C}q(j^{-1})=b_{Q,c}.$$
Since $t_C$ is invertible, solve this equality by multiplying by $(t_C^{-1})^\vee$. Substituting in step 3 gives
$$Vq(g)=g'(F'(u^{-1}))^\vee(t_C^{-1})^\vee b_{Q,c}=g'(w^{-1})^\vee b_{Q,c}.$$
The last equality is precomposition in reverse order: $w^{-1}=t_C^{-1}F'(u^{-1})$. This uses no inverse of $v$ and works for every stipulated $Q$, in particular for a compact-support comparison $u$.
